baseline.description: Protected Mesh and the stock Oban, River and Apalis workers. Each engine uses its original producer and default PostgreSQL storage.
baseline.title: Four-engine baseline

bulk-short.description: Both Mesh lanes run the same V2 grouped-success scheduler. The producer switches between set-based and scalar enqueue for the identical 128-job submission.
bulk-short.title: Trusted short jobs · batch enqueue and grouped settlements

bulk-slow.description: The same ordinary V1 executable switches between the batch and scalar producer. Each 512-job rotation includes the original trusted and protected Mesh builds and all three stock peers.
bulk-slow.title: Trusted slow jobs · set-based enqueue

current.description: Current and archived protected Mesh releases alongside stock River and Oban.
current.title: Protected Mesh rebuild

direct.description: The compiled Mesh producer reads and decodes the input file after submission. Two stock Mesh controls use the original broker. PostgreSQL uses its default storage for all four engines.
direct.title: Direct-file producer

lean.description: Four Mesh builds isolate the smaller fresh-exec worker, set-based claims, and the two changes together. Every job retains a fresh process and two fenced application commits.
lean.title: Protected worker and admission

ordinary.description: Ordinary Mesh handlers share a process and credentials and use application-owned PostgreSQL connections. Protected Mesh uses a fresh process and token-fenced writes. All four engines commit both writes independently.
ordinary.title: Trusted shared-process handlers · short

ordinary-cohort.description: Both ordinary Mesh arms use the same executable. One uses the original admission and settlement policy. The other claims jobs with a set-based query and can settle up to eight successful jobs in one transaction. Each job still has two independently committed application writes.
ordinary-cohort.title: Trusted handlers · grouped successful settlements

ordinary-dense.description: Eight runners share 64 slots. Ordinary Mesh handlers run in the application trust domain and make two independently committed writes. The protected control uses a fresh process and a fenced checkout per write.
ordinary-dense.title: Trusted shared-process handlers · dense

ordinary-large.description: Every engine stores the 64 submitted 512 KiB arguments with PostgreSQL EXTERNAL storage. The two Mesh arms use the same direct-file producer. Their handlers use either shared-process execution or a fresh process with fenced writes.
ordinary-large.title: Trusted shared-process handlers · large

ordinary-slow.description: One runner admits up to 64 jobs that each hold for 100 ms between their two application commits. All five arms consume the same 512 submitted jobs.
ordinary-slow.title: Trusted shared-process handlers · slow

ordinary-sparse.description: One runner and one slot serve 24 singleton arrivals at a five-connection cap, with a 250 ms gap after each settlement.
ordinary-sparse.title: Trusted shared-process handlers · sparse

persistent.description: The opt-in Mesh worker keeps its process across attempts. The parent owns the PostgreSQL credentials and fences both application calls. The strict Mesh control starts a fresh worker for each attempt.
persistent.title: Reusable, supervised worker processes

storage.description: The two tuned Mesh arms use PostgreSQL EXTERNAL storage for job arguments. The three peers use their default storage. Repeated-character payloads can use substantially more disk with EXTERNAL.
storage.title: Large payloads · Mesh storage tuning

strict-admission.description: Compare the original Mesh dispatcher with set-based claim admission on the same host as the peer engines. Both Mesh arms require confirmed claims, fresh workers, two fenced writes, and individual terminal commits.
strict-admission.title: Protected set-based admission

symmetric.description: Every engine stores the full 512 KiB payload with PostgreSQL EXTERNAL storage. Both protected Mesh arms process the same jobs with different producers.
symmetric.title: Large payloads · equal storage tuning

trusted-product.description: The public db5937e7 opt-in confirms actor teardown before settlement. Its matched control is the frozen ordinary V1 runner. Both use the same broker and CPU pair.
trusted-product.title: Product trusted execution and frozen V1

workmem-large.description: All engines run with EXTERNAL argument storage and 16 MiB PostgreSQL work_mem. Two additional Mesh controls retain 4 MiB. The same trusted Mesh binary runs all three Mesh lanes.
workmem-large.title: Large payloads · equal 16 MiB work_mem
